spans.text: the intentional regulation of the desire for food

description.value: Participants viewed high-caloric food images under ADMIT and REGULATE instructions and rated their performance.

spans.text: During the fMRI experiments, volunteers viewed every food image for 6 s under two conditions.
REGULATE_TASTY
The second condition (REGULATE)

description.value: Participants viewed three individually selected unhealthy, tasty high-calorie food images, each for 6 seconds, while intentionally downregulating their desire to eat by cognitively reinterpreting the food in terms of long-term negative health and social consequences; they then rated how well they completed the task on a 1-to-4 scale.

spans.text: The second condition (REGULATE) was indicated by the word ‘unterdrücken’ (suppress) and the associated instruction was to downregulate the desire for the following three food presentations by thinking about the long-term consequences of eating the food.
ADMIT_TASTY
The first condition (ADMIT)

description.value: Participants viewed three individually selected unhealthy, tasty high-calorie food images, each for 6 seconds, while intentionally admitting to their desire to eat the food; they then rated how well they completed the task on a 1-to-4 scale.

spans.text: The first condition (ADMIT) was indicated by visual presentation of the German word ‘zulassen’ (admit) and instructed the participant to admit to her desire to eat the food shown in the following three images.
ADMIT_NONTASTY
The first condition (ADMIT)

description.value: Participants viewed three individually selected unhealthy, non-tasty high-calorie food images, each for 6 seconds, while intentionally admitting to their desire to eat the food; they then rated how well they completed the task on a 1-to-4 scale.
